title: 14th Sitting of First session of 2026
presiding: Speaker Abdul Raheem Abdulla; Deputy Speaker Ahmed Nazim took the chair later in the sitting
summary: The sitting opened at 9:02 with routine business: the agenda, the minutes of sittings 8 to 10, and two chair announcements about committees. Members then spent most of the morning debating the government-backed bill to amend the Fisheries Act, with MPs from the governing side supporting it and arguing over fishers' prices, payments and past governments' records, while Mauroof Zakir questioned whether it answers fishers' real problems. After the chair closed that debate (a vote on the bill was due at the day's voting time) and a 30-minute recess, debate began on a resolution about how Public Service Media treats political parties; it was still going when this part ends. One speech in the Huvadhu dialect is only partly readable in the text. The part opens with the continuing debate on a resolution tabled by the South Galolhu member about how Public Service Media treats political parties; members from the governing side spoke against it and an MDP member for it, and the debate was paused for a one-hour recess without a vote. Parliament then took two committee reports and approved, by unanimous committee recommendation, the appointment of two non-resident ambassadors and the 14 cabinet ministers named by the President. In the vote round it accepted a Fisheries Act amendment bill for committee study, confirmed both ambassadors, and gave consent to all 14 ministers, most by wide margins. Parts of the text are garbled, so speaker stances are summarised loosely.

items.title: Attendance of members
items.outcome: 37 present, 6 on leave, 2 on official travel

items.title: Minutes of sittings 8 to 10 of 2026 (minutes no. 2026/1/8)
items.outcome: Accepted by the chair under rule 240 as no member proposed changes

items.title: Committee membership change announced by the chair
items.outcome: Asma Rasheed (Central Maafannu) replaces Mohamed Ali (Dhuvaafaru) on the Social Committee, PNC quota

items.title: Committee report deadline: bill to amend the Pension Act (No. 8/2009)
items.outcome: Independent Institutions Committee given 15 June 2026 to report

items.title: Bill to amend the Fisheries Act (No. 14/2019), sponsored by Mohamed Alsan Ahmed (South Thinadhoo)
items.outcome: Debated; chair closed debate, vote on accepting the bill to come at the day's voting time

items.title: Resolution on Public Service Media's treatment of political parties and editorial independence, proposed by Meekail Ahmed Nasym (South Galolhu)
items.outcome: Debate began; 30-minute recess; debate continuing at end of this part

items.title: Unfinished business: resolution on Public Service Media coverage of political parties (moved by the South Galolhu member)
items.outcome: debated by 7 members in this part; paused for 12:00-13:00 recess, no vote in this part

items.title: Foreign Relations Committee report on non-resident ambassadors to Cambodia/Vietnam and Greece
items.outcome: report presented; no member asked to speak; went to vote, both nominees approved

items.title: Government Accountability Committee report on consent for 14 ministers appointed by the President
items.outcome: report presented, one member supported it; went to vote, all 14 approved

items.title: Votes on pending matters
items.outcome: Fisheries Act amendment bill sent to Economic Committee; 2 ambassadors and 14 ministers approved

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Supported the fisheries amendment and thanked its sponsor.
Said government work for fishers should be backed and improved further.
Was reminded by the chair that the item was a fisheries bill, not a constitutional amendment.
Opposed the resolution, saying he found no breach of the state media or elections laws by Public Service Media.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said Public Service Media does not give MDP and others the equal opportunities the Public Service Media Act requires.
Argued citizens should hear both sides and Public Service Media should check claims it broadcasts.
Disputed a PNC claim about MDP-era borrowing, saying part of the debt cited was taken by the current government.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Supported the fisheries amendment and said fishers are now paid within 48 hours.
Claimed about 900 million rufiyaa owed to fishers went unpaid under the previous government.
On the resolution, said he did not support it and that Public Service Media gives MDP opportunities.
Opposed the resolution, saying Public Service Media covers opposition news in detail and that MDP declines its interview invitations.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Said earlier governments also failed to solve fisheries problems, so criticism after 2.5 years is unfair.
Raised export rejections at Bangkok and urged new markets such as Europe and the Americas.
Said the government is researching markets and supports the amendments.
Said attacks on the President and his family have gone too far, and cited media allowances passed by parliament as support for media freedom.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shameez
positions: Supported the amendment and thanked its sponsor.
Said fishers who took loans for boats face bank repayment pressure when they cannot sell fish at fair prices.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Said the bill has about 17 amendments, including releasing detained foreign vessels against a deposit.
Argued banks should offer special loans to fishers.
Urged sending the bill quickly to committee.
Supported the committee report on the 14 ministers, noting committee approval was unanimous and ministers have answered members' questions.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Backed the resolution, saying Public Service Media should scrutinise government pledges on payments to fishers.
Said it should report how much fish is in storage and where it is exported.
Was told by the chair to keep to the resolution's subject.

speakers.name: Ahmed Saleem
positions: Said Public Service Media's role is to inform citizens about government policy.
Noted parties now run their own TV channels, so access to information is wider.
Warned against media spreading unproven allegations that damage people's reputations.
Argued that attacking people's honour and spreading false claims in the media is wrong in Islam, and urged members to avoid defaming others.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Questioned whether the amendments answer fishers' main concerns, citing illegal foreign fishing in the economic zone.
Said promised prices for fishers and fuel support, especially for non-tuna fishers, are still unmet.
Argued the amendments could make Maldivian waters easier for foreign boats to use.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Supported the amendment, saying the industry weakened over time and the government is working to expand it.
Said young people now work on dinghies and need ways to earn a fair income.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Supported the amendment and compared the current government's fisheries record with the MDP's 2008 to 2018 record.
Said the government has set up faster payment and fuel arrangements for fishers.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Supported the amendment and defended the government's pledge on fish prices.
Said fuel at STO rates, cold storage and quick payment now exist, unlike under the previous government.

speakers.name: Ashraf Rasheed
positions: Supported the amendment and thanked its sponsor.
Said STO-rate fuel now reaches 13 atolls and payment comes within 48 hours.
Asked the government to restore a fishing boat arrangement for Faresmaathodaa.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Supported the amendment, saying it protects fishers when foreign vessels are detained.
Said the China free trade agreement could open larger markets for Maldivian fish.

speakers.name: Asadhulla Shihab
positions: Spoke in the Huvadhu dialect in support of the amendment and defended the government's record on fuel and fish prices.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Said public media should not be used to attack leaders or show frightening content, and said he would not support the resolution.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Opposed the resolution, arguing Public Service Media gives opposition parties space and pointing to media decisions made under the earlier MDP government.

speakers.name: Mohamed Dawoodh
positions: Presented the Foreign Relations Committee report recommending the two non-resident ambassador appointments, passed unanimously in committee.

speakers.name: Ali Fazad
positions: Presented the Government Accountability Committee report recommending consent for 14 ministers after checking constitutional eligibility and agency records.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Supported the proposal, saying state-linked media has not given the opposition equal and fair space and should present news evenly.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 8 to 10 of 2026 declared accepted as no member proposed amendments.
Asma Rasheed (Central Maafannu) placed on the Social Committee in place of Mohamed Ali (Dhuvaafaru).
Independent Institutions Committee given 15 June 2026 to report on the Pension Act amendment bill.
Debate on the Fisheries Act amendment bill closed; the chair said members would be asked at the day's voting time whether to accept the bill.
Deputy Speaker Ahmed Nazim took the chair; 30-minute recess before debate on the Public Service Media resolution resumed.
Debate on the Public Service Media resolution was paused for a recess (12:00-13:00) with no vote in this part.
Fisheries Act (14/2019) amendment bill, proposed by the government via South Thinadhoo's Mohamed Alsan Ahmed, accepted and sent to the Economic Committee.
Mariyam Mifga Naeem approved as non-resident ambassador to Cambodia and Vietnam.
Hassan Adam approved as non-resident ambassador to Greece.

Consent given to 14 ministers: Finance and Public Enterprises, Homeland Security Labour and Technology, Foreign Affairs, Education, Health, Economic Development, Islamic Affairs, Tourism, Youth, Arts and Culture, Infrastructure, Climate and Environment, Defence, Fisheries.
Next sitting set for Monday 4 May 2026 at 9:00.
